purpose: Dated 2006 offseason facts: lottery, early-entry application and withdrawal deadlines, the pre-draft camp, draft, option and qualifying-offer deadline, the July moratorium, cap publication, the 2006-07 cap, tax level, floor, exceptions, minimum, maximum and first-round rookie scales, 2006-07 opening day and the 30-team alignment. The 2005 agreement is in force all summer (no new agreement, no amnesty). A cap figure is live only from its publication date (July 11, 2006); the minimum, maximum floor and rookie scales and the Bi-Annual amount were fixed in the 2005 agreement and public from its ratification (July 30, 2005).

finals_2006.value: NBA Finals scheduled June 8-22, 2006 (2-3-2; Game 7, if needed, June 22)
finals_2006.note: The window only. The real 2006 Finals result is deliberately not recorded: the simulation plays its own 2006 playoffs, and the real result involves real Miami, whose results are never applied (AGENTS.md).

expansion_draft.note: No expansion draft in 2006: Charlotte's 2004 expansion draft was the only one of this era (Wikipedia lists 2004 as the last expansion draft).

early_entry_application_deadline.note: A player not automatically eligible declares in writing no later than 60 days before the draft (June 28 less 60 days = April 29). Under the 2005 agreement's age rule a U.S. player must be 19 during 2006 and one year past his high-school class; no high-school player was eligible.
early_entry_application_deadline.status: sourced (secondary: rule and the April 29 date)
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NBA_draft (Eligibility: 'no later than 60 days before the draft')

https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2006/4/7/josh_boone_declares_for_2006_nba_draft_but_will_not_hire_agent (University of Connecticut, April 7, 2006: deadline for underclassmen to declare April 29; read through a search-engine extract, the page itself returned 403)

predraft_camp.note: Camp games began Tuesday June 6 (three games), with a second tripleheader Thursday June 8; the third-day report (dated June 10) says the camp had concluded. The last day is derived from those reports. Measurements taken at the camp are pre-draft evidence from their camp date (another file).
sources: https://www.hoopville.com/2006/06/08/orlando-pre-draft-camp-day-one/ ('kicked off in its new digs with three games on Tuesday'; 'Thursday offers up a 2nd tripleheader')

early_entry_withdrawal_deadline.time: 1 p.m. (per report; time zone not stated)
early_entry_withdrawal_deadline.note: Sunday June 18, ten days before the draft: early-entry candidates who had not signed with an agent could withdraw in writing and keep college eligibility. The 2005 deadline was June 21 (the 2005 file); the 2006 rule is ten days before the draft.
sources: https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/wbna12557111 (Washington Post, Eric Prisbell, April 30, 2006: players without agents may return to school 'by pulling out of the draft before the June 18 deadline')
https://www.memphisflyer.com/?p=1126049 (Memphis Flyer, April 30, 2006: 'have until June 18th to change their mind')
https://dailybruin.com/2006/06/16/bonline-exclusiveb-afflalo-wit/ (Daily Bruin, June 16, 2006: 'the 1 p.m. deadline on Sunday')
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NBA_draft (Eligibility: withdrawal 'no later than 10 days before the draft')

early_entry_final_list.note: The NBA announced the early-entry candidates who stayed in the draft after the withdrawal deadline (37 college players and 10 international players; 47 earlier candidates withdrew). This list, as of the deadline, is the class's identity (the class file); the counts are recorded here only as the announcement's content.
early_entry_final_list.status: sourced (secondary: Wikipedia citing the NBA.com announcement)
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_NBA_draft (Eligibility: 'On June 19, 2006, NBA announced that 37 college players and 10 international players had filed as early-entry candidates')

draft.location: The Theater at Madison Square Garden, New York City

options_and_qualifying_offers_deadline.note: Team and player option decisions and qualifying offers that make a player a restricted free agent are due June 30, the last day of the league year, under the 2005 agreement. No 2006-specific notice moving the date was found, but none confirming it either.
options_and_qualifying_offers_deadline.status: sourced (rule: cbafaq05 Q37, qualifying offer due June 30); 2006-specific confirmation unverified

free_agency_negotiation_opens.note: Free agents become free July 1; during the moratorium teams may negotiate but not sign (except required tenders, qualifying offers, first-round scale signings and second-round minimum signings).

july_moratorium.note: The ordinary moratorium: it ends when the cap is set from the audit (the 2005 extension to August 1 does not recur). Teams were told the 2006-07 figures late Tuesday July 11 and the moratorium was lifted at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday July 12.
sources: http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap05.htm (Q93: 2006-07, 'July 1, 2006 through July 11, 2006', players may be signed beginning July 12, 2006)

cap_published.note: The 2006-07 cap, tax level and Mid-Level amount reached the clubs late Tuesday July 11, 2006. A reader gating live use treats them as known from July 11 and effective from July 12 (runtime/free_agency_2004.py takes the day before the first signing day).

amnesty_window_2006.note: No amnesty in 2006: the 2005 agreement's luxury-tax amnesty waiver was a one-time window (August 2-15, 2005).

salary_cap_2006_07.effective: 2006-07-12 (the cap adjusts on the first day after the July moratorium)
salary_cap_2006_07.note: 51% of projected Basketball Related Income less projected benefits, divided by the clubs (the 2005 agreement's formula from 2006-07; 49.5% and a fixed figure in 2005-06).
sources: https://www.sportsbookreview.com/forum/nba-basketball-betting/10416-salary-cap-for-2006-07-season-set-at-53-135m (forum repost dated 07-11-06, 11:11 PM, of a July 11, 2006 wire report: 'NBA teams received word late Tuesday on the new numbers')

luxury_tax_threshold_2006_07.note: Set before the season with the cap (61% of projected BRI less benefits, divided by the clubs) and levied every season on team salary at the club's last regular-season game. Published with the cap on July 11, 2006. The FAQ's list of real 2006-07 taxpaying clubs is hindsight and is not recorded.
sources: https://www.sportsbookreview.com/forum/nba-basketball-betting/10416-salary-cap-for-2006-07-season-set-at-53-135m (forum repost dated 07-11-06, 11:11 PM, of a July 11, 2006 wire report: 'NBA teams received word late Tuesday on the new numbers') ('The luxury tax threshold will be $65.42 million')

salary_floor_2006_07.note: 75% of the $53.135 million cap (minimum team salary percentage sourced in cbafaq05 Q10); the dollar figure itself is computed.

charlotte_cap_and_floor_2006_07.note: Charlotte's third season: the expansion club's own reduced cap applied to its first two seasons only (the cap is computed 'excluding expansion teams in their first two seasons'), so in 2006-07 Charlotte has the league cap and floor. Recorded with the league figures so a reader of the 2004 and 2005 shape sees no reduced cap.
sources: http://www.cbafaq.com/salarycap05.htm (Q10: 'excluding expansion teams in their first two seasons'; only 2005-06 lists a Charlotte figure)

mid_level_exception_2006_07.note: Defined as the average salary, so the figure is set at the start of the signing period; up to 5 years, 8% raises.
sources: https://www.sportsbookreview.com/forum/nba-basketball-betting/10416-salary-cap-for-2006-07-season-set-at-53-135m (forum repost dated 07-11-06, 11:11 PM, of a July 11, 2006 wire report: 'NBA teams received word late Tuesday on the new numbers') ('can sign contracts beginning at $5.215 million annually')

one_million_exception_2006_07.note: The Bi-Annual exception (formerly the $1 Million exception); same figure as bi_annual_exception_2006_07, key kept for the 2004 naming. Up to 2 years, 8% raises; not usable by a club that used it in 2005-06.

bi_annual_exception_2006_07.note: A fixed amount in the 2005 agreement (2005-06 $1.67 million, 2006-07 $1.75 million), public from ratification.

minimum_salary_scale_2006_07.note: Fixed in the 2005 agreement for every season and public from its ratification. The league reimburses one-year minimum contracts of 3+-year veterans above the 2-year minimum, and only the 2-year minimum counts on team salary. Values for 0, 1, 2 and 10+ years match nba_2006_07_cap_rules.json (RealGM).

maximum_salary_2006_07.note: 25%, 30% and 35% of the 2005 agreement's maximum-salary base (48.04% of projected Basketball Related Income, below the cap's 51%), published with the cap (the report rounds them to $12.45, $14.94 and $17.43 million). The summer market reads them from the 2006 summer (runtime/free_agency_2004.calendar, `maximum`), priced with the cap they were published with, in place of the agreement's share of the cap ($13,283,750, $15,940,500 and $18,597,250).
sources: https://www.sportsbookreview.com/forum/nba-basketball-betting/10416-salary-cap-for-2006-07-season-set-at-53-135m (forum repost dated 07-11-06, 11:11 PM, of a July 11, 2006 wire report: 'NBA teams received word late Tuesday on the new numbers')

rookie_scale_2006_first_round.note: Scale amounts for players drafted in 2006 (2005 agreement, 2006-07 table, fixed when the agreement was written). Actual contracts may be 80%-120% of scale. Years 1 and 2 are guaranteed; year 3 is a team option exercised by October 31 before the second season and year 4 a team option exercised by October 31 before the third season; year4_option_raise_pct is the required raise of year 4 over year 3 and qualifying_offer_raise_pct the qualifying offer's raise over year 4 (the same percentages as 2005). Every amount is 3.70% above the 2005-06 amount for the same pick. Pick 11's first year is recorded as $1,550,600: the source prints $550,600, a dropped digit (the 3.70% step from 2005-06's $1,495,200 and the 7.5% year-2 step to $1,666,800 both give $1,550,600, and the source's own signed-percentage column, 338% of $550,600, equals 120% of $1,550,600). Pick 1 matches Coon's FAQ.
rookie_scale_2006_first_round.status: sourced (full table: SalarySwish 2006-07 rookie scale, a secondary transcription of CBA Exhibit B; pick 11 year 1 corrected, derived); pick 1 cross-checked against cbafaq05 Q42

cba_term_note.value: The 2005 CBA (ratified July 30, 2005; effective August 2, 2005) runs six seasons, 2005-06 through 2010-11, with a league option for 2011-12; the 2006 offseason is its second and has no agreement event. 2006-07 figures above are under it.

alignment_2006_07.note: Same membership as 2005-06. The Hornets are still the New Orleans/Oklahoma City Hornets (NOK, the code of library/2006/league/nba_2006_07_team_rosters.json) for 2006-07, and the 2006 draft is the only one they made under that name. Listed alphabetically; the source page orders by final 2006-07 standings (hindsight), which was deliberately not carried over.

notes: HINDSIGHT WARNING: Coon's FAQ lists later-season caps, tax levels and real taxpaying clubs, and the cap report describes real clubs' July 2006 spending; none of these were copied. Only 2006-07 figures and dated rules are recorded, each live from its own date.
HINDSIGHT WARNING: the real 2006 Finals result, lottery result, draft order and picks are not recorded; the Finals entry carries the scheduled window only.

The minimum and maximum-floor scales, the Bi-Annual amount and the rookie scale were fixed in the 2005 agreement and were public from its ratification (July 30, 2005); the cap, tax level and Mid-Level amount are knowable only from July 11, 2006.
web.archive.org was not used; NBA.com's 2006 releases (lottery, early-entry list, cap) are cited through Wikipedia and contemporaneous reports.
